records.title: Fetichism in West Africa
records.translator: not applicable; authored in English by Robert Hamill Nassau
records.rightsStatus: Project Gutenberg public-domain edition; preserve attribution and review UK reuse before redistribution.
records.notes: Nassau was a missionary in the Gabun District of French Congo. His book is a colonial-era ethnographic synthesis with only incidental, second-hand Yoruba references; it is not a Yoruba community source.

records.title: Folk Stories from Southern Nigeria
ancientAuthors: Various southern Nigerian storytellers; collected and retold in English by Elphinstone Dayrell
records.rightsStatus: Project Gutenberg public-domain edition; preserve attribution and review UK reuse before redistribution.
records.notes: A colonial-era English collection titled for Southern Nigeria that does not consistently identify the specific community for each story; do not label its tales Yoruba without additional provenance.

records.title: The Yoruba-Speaking Peoples of the Slave Coast of West Africa
records.translator: not applicable; authored in English by A. B. Ellis
records.rightsStatus: First published 1894; public domain in the United States. Transcription via the Internet Sacred Text Archive; preserve attribution.
records.notes: Ellis was a British colonial officer; this 1894 survey is specifically about the Yoruba-speaking peoples of the Slave Coast, unlike Nassau's wider synthesis. It remains colonial-era ethnography with dated interpretations: attribute claims to Ellis's report, keep his comparative and evolutionary frameworks visible as commentary, and do not treat it as community testimony. The transcription omits chapters X-XII (government, laws, language).

records.title: Yoruba Legends
ancientAuthors: Yoruba storytellers; collected and published in English by M. I. Ogumefu
records.translator: not applicable; authored in English by M. I. Ogumefu
records.rightsStatus: First published 1929; public domain in the United States as a pre-1930 work. Author's death date is unverified, so review UK/EU reuse before redistribution. Transcription via the Internet Sacred Text Archive; preserve attribution.
records.notes: A Yoruba-authored English collection of forty legends, explicitly framed by Ogumefu as belonging to "the Yoruba country of Southern Nigeria." The preface shows a mission-era Christian framing alongside pride in the tales; keep both visible. Nine tales form a dedicated Tortoise cycle.
